Need to search first.I don't have any notes to give you this time, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

My first attempt to open pages directly (Enduring Word on Jeremiah 48, and the biblehub.com commentary pages for vv. 26, 31, 40, 45 and 47) was blocked. The tool only opens pages that a search has turned up first. When I then ran the searches, I had already hit my tool-use limit for this turn, so nothing came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. With nothing read, writing notes on Jeremiah 48:25–47 would mean making them up, so I haven't.

**What I'll do if you ask again (for example, "please try again"):**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word's Jeremiah 48 page, the biblehub.com and studylight.org pages for each verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry and others), and preceptaustin.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** check the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites. I'd focus on the verses most likely to divide them:
   - God's own lament over Moab (vv. 31–32, 36)
   - what the "drunkenness" image means (v. 26)
   - how to understand the restoration "in the latter days" (v. 47)
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes on the harder phrases, such as the "sons of tumult" (v. 45) and Eglath-shelishiyah (v. 34)
   - Bible Odyssey on Moab and Chemosh
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings of v. 47
   - popular modern teaching, but only if those sites actually discuss it

If the tool limit makes one pass too long, I can split the work into vv. 25–35 and then vv. 36–47.
